title: Upgrade risk report
summary: An engineering lead must decide by Friday whether to upgrade nine services before a code freeze or push everything to January. The input is the platform team's notes, a service dependency inventory and a quarter of incident records.
inputs: the platform team's notes: staging results, estimates, constraints
look_for: A verdict with a glyph, a confidence line and its basis, then three decisions that each say who, what, by when and what is recommended.
A ranked risk table with a severity glyph and a link from every risk to the section that handles it.
A dependency map of the nine services with the hub highlighted, built as an image so it renders everywhere, with its source file beside it.
The raw incident rows and checksummed copies of the inputs in a collapsed archive zone, because the user asked to keep the supporting data.

title: Dual-audience handoff
summary: An engineer goes on leave. A manager will skim the handoff; an AI agent will continue the work from it. The input is a work log, a task list and a list of open questions.
inputs: six questions that need other people
look_for: One document with two readers: a human panel for the manager (status, blockers, decisions) and a self-sufficient AI-input block for the agent (paths, commands, constraints, what not to do, definition of done).
A task dependency graph that shows which blockers stop which tasks.
Decisions that say when the source gives no deadline instead of inventing one, and suggested dates marked as suggested.

title: Platform explainer for a new hire
summary: A new engineer needs to understand how a file upload becomes a published table on an ingestion platform with eleven components. The input is architecture notes and an onboarding checklist.
inputs: an unedited brain dump: components, concepts, numbers, failure handling, gotchas
what the new hire should do in week one
look_for: No verdict to invent: the first screen opens with the mental model as one sentence, then a picture and the handful of things that matter, each with the trap if it is missed.
A glossary placed before the first section that uses its terms (concepts before flows).
A component map with eleven nodes that stays legible because it is split into an overview and a zoom.

title: Post-mortem in Chinese
summary: A production outage has been handled. The tech lead must decide which follow-up items to do first. The request, the notes and the raw chat log are all in Chinese, and the raw chat log must stay in the report.
inputs: the raw group chat during the incident
look_for: The document, its headings, labels and diagram text are in the reader's language, with no empty glyph boxes in the picture (the skill documents the CJK font pitfall).
A root cause with confidence and basis, the impact, and the decision the tech lead has to take, all on the first screen.
The raw chat log preserved in a collapsed archive block.
